questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows a production possibility diagram for an economy where goods and services are produced in the private and public sectors. The economy is currently producing at point Y. Following a change in government, it is decided that the output of public sector goods and services should be increased by VW. What is the opportunity cost, in terms of private sector output, of this reallocation of resources?
options: OS
OT
ST
YZ

questions.questionText: Country X and Country Y have identical amounts of the factors of production that can be used to produce either canoes or rowing boats. Figure 7 shows the production possibility frontiers (PPFs) for the two countries. Which one of the following is supported by the data in Figure 7?
options: Country X has both an absolute advantage and a comparative advantage in producing canoes
In Country Y, the production of rowing boats requires two and a half times as many resources as the production of canoes
The maximum number of canoes and rowing boats that Country X and Country Y can produce between them is 400
The opportunity cost of producing a canoe in Country Y is 25% lower than it is in Country X

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the production possibility boundary for petrol-powered cars and electric-powered cars in a country's car industry. If production has moved from Point A to Point B, which one of the following must be true?
options: Allocative efficiency in the car industry is unchanged
Demand for electric-powered vehicles has increased
Productive efficiency in the car industry is unchanged
Static efficiency in the car industry has improved

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the production possibility diagram for an economy producing capital goods and consumer goods. The opportunity cost of producing an additional unit of capital goods is
options: greater at X than Y.
greater at Z than Y.
the same at X, Y and Z.
zero when 300 units of consumer goods are produced.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the production possibility curve for an economy producing capital and consumer goods. The opportunity cost of increasing the output of capital goods from G1 to G2 is shown by
options: H - H2
H2KLH1
G2 - G1
H1 - H2

questions.questionText: Explain how a production possibility diagram can be used to illustrate some features of the fundamental economic problem.

The diagram below shows the production possibility frontier for an economy that produces consumer goods and capital goods. The economy is initially operating at point X within its frontier. If the economy now moves from point X to point Y on its frontier it will
options: achieve both productive and allocative efficiency.
benefit from improved economies of scale in the production of both goods.
increase its underlying trend rate of growth.
obtain more consumer goods and capital goods at zero opportunity cost.
